From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.example>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-11-07T13:26:40-08:00
Subject: Re: Degraded responses / 502s across prod (us-west)

Quick update from the bridge:
- Root cause hypothesis: a recent autoscaler heuristic permitted a small set of pods to drop below desired capacity during a short CPU spike; KV cache misses amplified cold-path invocations on the host and exhausted a GPU worker queue for ~3m windows leading to 502s.
- Short-term mitigation applied: forced restart of 3 affected nodes + throttled public burst routing for 10m; 5xx rate dropped from ~8% -> ~1.2% within two minutes of action.
- Next step: redistribute active shard allocation and increase minimum replica target for the us-west pool; planned rollback window: 13:40-14:00.

I'll take the exec-facing language for the note, Irene. Marcus

Marcus Lin
Director, Runtime Reliability | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.example

Attachments: api-trace-sample.log

Thanks — confirmation from our side: affected traffic is primarily us-west; we saw a 2-minute window of retries from our client fallback earlier but no config changes on our side. Billing/observability team also confirmed those request IDs map to checkout path only.

Appreciate the immediate action and the bridge. We'll keep monitoring and can provide request traces as you need. Our CTO wanted a short note for leadership — please include estimated user impact and expected timeline to full restoral.

Alyssa

Date: 2027-11-09T09:17:00-08:00
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — Bytefront (Incident BRG-9241)

Hi Alyssa —

Appreciate the collaboration on BRG-9241. This note summarizes what happened, the immediate mitigations we took, and our follow-ups. Please let me know if you want anything added for your leadership.

Incident summary (short):
- Impact: 5xx errors (primarily 502) observed in the us-west generation pool between 2027-11-07 12:45 — 13:15 PDT; user-facing errors on checkout estimated at ~6% of attempts during the peak window.
- Root cause (preliminary): autoscaler heuristic + cache miss amplification resulted in transient worker queue exhaustion on a subset of nodes.

Immediate mitigation and timeline:
- 13:10 PDT: Bridge stood up (BRG-9241).
- 13:14 PDT: Forced restart of 3 affected nodes and temporary routing throttles applied. 5xx rate reduced to ~1.2% by 13:16.
- 13:28 PDT: Shard redistribution and minimum replica increase completed; service stabilized and noise returned to baseline.

Customer impact:
- Affected customers: Bytefront (checkout path).
- Duration of elevated error rate: ~30 minutes.
- Estimated user-facing failure rate at peak: ~6%

Follow-up actions (owner / ETA):
- Adjust autoscaler heuristics to avoid sub-minimum scaling during CPU spikes — Marcus Lin / 2027-11-14
- Add a quick KV cache warm-up to reduce cold-path amplification — Marcus Lin / 2027-11-10
- Share final postmortem and timeline with Bytefront — Irene Choi / 2027-11-12
- Provide request-trace bundle for Bytefront debug team — Jordan Blake / 2027-11-08 (sent)

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md (internal draft), incident-runbook.pdf, api-trace-sample.log

If you want a short one-pager for your CTO, I can draft it this morning; otherwise, expect our formal postmortem by 2027-11-12.

Thanks again for the quick collaboration.

Irene Choi
